title: Deleting a user keeps their articles and sets author_id to NULL.
content:
The articles.author_id foreign key uses ondelete SET NULL and is nullable, while comments, favorites and follows use CASCADE. Articles can therefore exist without an author.
Source: app/app/db/migrations/versions/fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py:108

title: Article lists default to 20 items and have no upper limit.
content:
DEFAULT_ARTICLES_LIMIT is 20 and the limit query parameter is only constrained by ge=1, with no maximum. A client can request any page size.
Source: app/app/models/schemas/articles.py:8

title: Bad tokens, wrong prefixes and unknown users are answered with 403, not 401.
content:
_get_authorization_header and _get_current_user raise HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN for a malformed header, a wrong prefix, an undecodable token and a user that no longer exists. Clients see 403 for every authentication failure of a present header.
Source: app/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py:54

title: The Authorization header must use the prefix Token, not Bearer.
content:
AppSettings sets jwt_token_prefix to Token. _get_authorization_header splits the header on a space and rejects any prefix that does not match this setting.
Source: app/app/core/settings/app.py:29

title: Only the author may update or delete an article, checked by comparing usernames.
content:
check_user_can_modify_article compares the article author username with the current user username. check_article_modification_permissions raises 403 when they differ and guards the PUT and DELETE routes.
Source: app/app/services/articles.py:23

title: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt through a passlib CryptContext.
content:
security.py builds a CryptContext with the bcrypt scheme and deprecated set to auto, and uses it to hash and verify passwords.
Source: app/app/services/security.py:4

title: API models use camelCase JSON aliases generated from snake_case field names.
content:
RWModel sets alias_generator to convert_field_to_camel_case and allows population by field name. Renaming a Python field changes the public JSON key.
Source: app/app/models/domain/rwmodel.py:21

title: CORS allows every origin by default, with credentials allowed.
content:
AppSettings sets allowed_hosts to ["*"] and main.py passes it as allow_origins to CORSMiddleware with allow_credentials=True and all methods and headers.
Source: app/app/core/settings/app.py:31

title: Datetimes are serialized as UTC ISO strings ending in Z.
content:
convert_datetime_to_realworld forces the UTC timezone and replaces +00:00 with Z; RWModel registers it as the datetime JSON encoder. It overwrites any existing tzinfo rather than converting it.
Source: app/app/models/domain/rwmodel.py:7

title: Creating an article whose title gives an existing slug is rejected with 400.
content:
create_new_article computes the slug and calls check_article_exists; if it exists the route raises 400 ARTICLE_ALREADY_EXISTS instead of making the slug unique with a suffix.
Source: app/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:65

title: Access tokens are signed with the symmetric HS256 algorithm.
content:
app/services/jwt.py sets ALGORITHM to HS256 and uses it both to encode and to decode tokens with the single secret_key. Changing the algorithm, or the key, invalidates every issued token.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:11

title: Access tokens expire after one week and there is no refresh token.
content:
ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES is 60 * 24 * 7 and create_access_token_for_user uses it as the expiry delta. No refresh or revocation mechanism exists in the code.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:12

title: The token identifies the user by username, not by user id.
content:
create_access_token_for_user puts only the username in the payload, and _get_current_user looks the user up by that username. Renaming a user makes old tokens fail, so the update-user route issues a new token.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:29

title: Login returns the same error for an unknown email and a wrong password.
content:
The login route builds one wrong_login_error and raises it both when the email lookup fails and when check_password fails. Both cases return 400 with INCORRECT_LOGIN_INPUT.
Source: app/app/api/routes/authentication.py:28

title: A separately stored per-user salt is prepended to the password before hashing.
content:
UserInDB.change_password generates a salt, stores it in the salt column, and hashes salt + password. check_password must prepend the same salt, so the salt column and the hash must change together.
Source: app/app/models/domain/users.py:24

title: Database access uses raw SQL files loaded with aiosql on asyncpg, not an ORM.
content:
queries.py loads every .sql file in app/db/queries/sql with the asyncpg adapter, and repositories call these named queries. Only filter_articles builds SQL dynamically with pypika.
Source: app/app/db/queries/queries.py:5

title: Updating an article title regenerates its slug, so its URL changes.
content:
update_article_by_slug recomputes the slug from the new title when a title is given and passes it to the repository as new_slug. Unlike creation, this path does not check for an existing slug first.
Source: app/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:100

title: An article slug is derived from its title with slugify.
content:
get_slug_for_article returns slugify(title). The slug is the public identifier used in every article URL and is unique in the articles table.
Source: app/app/services/articles.py:19

title: updated_at is maintained by a Postgres trigger, not by application code.
content:
The migration creates the plpgsql function update_updated_at_column and BEFORE UPDATE triggers on users, articles and commentaries that set updated_at to now().
Source: app/app/db/migrations/versions/fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py:27
